en.title: Still low-cost? How Southwest Airlines and JetBlue compare in 2026
en.summary: Neither Southwest nor JetBlue is really a low-cost carrier any more: both are now hybrid carriers, with JetBlue leading on seats and the onboard experience and Southwest winning on domestic network scale, but both have had to reshape their business models to make money after COVID.
body: JetBlue and Southwest Airlines are two of the most unusual low-cost carriers in the United States, largely because neither is exactly low-cost. JetBlue pioneered seatback screens and free Wi-Fi across its fleet, along with lie-flat business class seats and transatlantic flights, while Southwest built its reputation on excellent service and generous customer policies, some of which have changed recently. Today both can comfortably be called hybrid carriers, blending the low-cost business model with elements of a full-service passenger experience.

Premium seating shows how far each has moved. Southwest completed a fleetwide retrofit of extra-legroom seats in January 2026, with 42 on its 737-700s and 48 on its 737-800s and 737 MAX 8s — a major step for an airline that long sold only standard economy seats. JetBlue has offered extra-legroom seats since 2008, rebranded as EvenMore in 2025, launched its lie-flat Mint business class in 2014, and will debut BlueFirst, a domestic first class cabin with recliners, in December, retrofitting it onto every non-Mint aircraft.

Policies and cabins tell a different story. Southwest ended its open-seating policy and its two-free-checked-bags policy because they left money on the table, and its cabins remain fairly basic, with standard legroom, no screens and no power ports on some aircraft. JetBlue has long offered better economy pitch, seatback screens on all aircraft and free Wi-Fi since 2013, along with more generous snacks and larger meals — but its BlueFirst retrofits will cut economy legroom to the industry standard of 30 inches (76.2 centimeters).

On networks, JetBlue operates more than 300 aircraft from hubs in New York, Boston, Fort Lauderdale, Orlando and San Juan, but has a very small West Coast presence and faces stiff competition from Delta in the Northeast. Southwest runs no long-haul or premium transcontinental flights, yet operates 13 bases across the country and carries nearly as many domestic passengers as American, Delta or United. After Elliott Investment Management took a major stake, Southwest has modernized its IT systems, added overnight flights, introduced seat assignment fees and started charging for checked luggage. JetBlue, meanwhile, has recorded losses since COVID and, despite its JetForward turnaround plan, still loses money; some, including founder and former CEO David Neeleman, have speculated it could head for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

zh.title: 西南航空與捷藍航空還是廉航嗎？兩家業者2026年比較
zh.summary: 西南航空與捷藍航空都不再是典型的廉價航空，兩家業者如今都可歸類為混合型航空公司：捷藍航空以座椅與機上體驗見長，西南航空則以國內航網規模取勝，但兩家業者都在疫情後調整商業模式以求獲利。
body: 捷藍航空與西南航空是美國兩家最具特色的廉價航空，但嚴格來說，兩家業者如今都算不上純粹的廉價航空。捷藍航空率先在全機隊導入座椅螢幕與免費無線網路，也推出平躺式商務艙Mint與跨大西洋航線；西南航空則以優質服務與寬鬆的旅客政策著稱，儘管部分政策近期已有改變。如今兩家業者都可以歸類為混合型航空公司，結合廉價航空的營運模式與全服務航空的搭乘體驗。

座椅產品的差距最能說明兩家業者的定位。西南航空在2026年1月完成全機隊加裝加大腿部空間座椅的改裝，737-700有42個這類座位，737-800與737MAX8則有48個，這是西南航空首次大規模銷售標準經濟艙以外的座位產品。捷藍航空早在2008年就提供加大腿部空間座位，2014年推出平躺式商務艙Mint，2025年將加大腿部空間座位更名為EvenMore，並將於12月推出國內線頭等艙BlueFirst，逐步改裝至所有非Mint機隊。
政策與航網則呈現另一種對比。西南航空過去以自由選位與兩件免費託運行李聞名，但兩項政策都已取消，因為它們讓業者少賺了不少收入；機艙內部相對樸素，部分飛機沒有螢幕與電源插座。捷藍航空的經濟艙腿部空間一向較寬敞，全機隊都有座椅螢幕，自2013年起提供免費無線網路，餐飲也比西南航空豐富；但捷藍航空近年為改裝BlueFirst，將經濟艙腿部空間縮減至業界標準的30英寸。

航網規模上，捷藍航空擁有超過300架飛機，樞紐集中於紐約、波士頓、羅德岱堡、奧蘭多與聖胡安，東北部實力堅強，但西岸據點很少，在全美多數地區缺乏存在感。西南航空沒有長程與高級跨大陸航線，但在全美設有13個營運基地，國內航網規模龐大，國內載客量幾乎與美國航空、達美航空或聯合航空相當。疫情後，西南航空在Elliott Investment Management入股後推動改革，包括導入紅眼航班、座位收費與託運行李收費；捷藍航空則持續虧損，創辦人兼前執行長David Neeleman等人已揣測其可能走向破產保護，BlueFirst能否扭轉局勢仍待觀察。
